For the second statement, average the differences x −VsFKVs−1x, each of which belongs to K, and then use conjugation invariance. These two properties imply P 2 K = PK and ker PK = K: apply PK to x−PKx ∈K, and conversely use that same inclusion when PKx = 0. Reindexing the finite group sum proves signed equivariance; the real average proves conjugation equivariance. Its norm is bounded by (CVP2) times the fixed finite average of ∥Vs∥∥Vs−1∥. The real average does not enlarge that bound, because conjugation is isometric in the frame coordinates. At the finitely many cutoffs where the calibrated symmetry has not yet been established, use (CVP1) instead. This supplies a uniform bound at every cutoffand the required exact symmetries on the admitted tail.
